entries.subject: HYG v4.4 stellar database
entries.finding: All 109,389 locally vendored HYG rows by David Nash / Astronexus, licensed CC-BY-SA-4.0, supply the field; every source row survives at its recorded Sun-origin ICRS Cartesian parsec position, and the README states this is a local neighbourhood within 991 pc, not a complete Milky Way census.

entries.subject: Proper-motion propagation to the navigation epoch
entries.finding: Catalogue astrometry is preserved without proper-motion propagation to the navigation epoch, with the source epochs and modifications kept in the pinned provenance.
entries.revisitWhen: The scene needs positions at an epoch far enough from the catalogue epoch for proper motion to matter visibly.

entries.subject: Fixed 2,048 active and 2,048 transition point slots
entries.finding: The fixed slots retain the complete dataset but may retire fainter visible rows when the point budget is saturated; the recorded projected-error statistic reports that condition.
entries.revisitWhen: The point budget grows or a selection rule keeps every visible row within budget.

entries.subject: int16 absolute-magnitude storage in the prepared bank
entries.finding: Absolute magnitudes ship as int16 decoded as float32(q/1000) with a declared bound of 5e-4 mag; 3.6e-4 mag was measured on 2 of 109,389 rows and 0 on the rest, and preparation fails if the measured error or its at most 1.09e-3 alpha effect exceeds the bound.

entries.subject: Fixed-point star positions
entries.finding: Positions stay float32 because the camera can approach any star, so a fixed-point position would eventually move visibly, and int32 fixed point would cost the same four bytes as the lossless float32 value.
entries.revisitWhen: A position encoding is found that is both lossless at close approach and smaller than float32.

entries.subject: Compressing the star bank at rest
entries.finding: The bank ships uncompressed because the dev server sends application/octet-stream without Content-Encoding and gzip at rest would not be byte-reproducible across zlib builds; hosts that compress octet streams reduce it further.
entries.revisitWhen: A compression at rest becomes byte-reproducible across zlib builds, or the host contract changes.
